supported-frameworks.statement: Risk360 supports these risk frameworks: ISO 27001, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, DORA, NIS2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, CIS, CAF, HITRUST, HECVAT, SOC 2 and GDPR.

quotes: The Risk360 service supports the following risk frameworks (Analytics > Risk360 > [select a framework]):
The ISO 27001 is a set of standards for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an information security management system (ISMS) for any organization.
MITRE ATT&CK is a cybersecurity framework funded by the US government
The Risk360 service supports both versions of NIST CSF (1.1 and 2.0) in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Special Publication (SP) 800-53 is a set of structured security and privacy controls
The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), a European Union (EU) regulation for the financial sector
The Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2) is a European Union (EU) law
The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) is a mandatory compliance framework
The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) is a mandatory security framework
The Center for Internet Security (CIS) Critical Security Controls are a prescriptive
The Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) is a standardized, outcome-focused compliance
The HITRUST compliance is a comprehensive and certifiable security framework
The Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) is developed by EDUCAUSE
System and Organization Controls 2 is a compliance standard for organizations that handle customer data
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a European Union (EU) regulation

nist-versions.statement: Risk360 supports both NIST CSF versions, 1.1 and 2.0, in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: The Risk360 service supports both versions of NIST CSF (1.1 and 2.0) in the Zscaler Admin Console.

framework-page-colors.statement: On a framework page each tile shows a technique name and ID; blue tiles are covered by Zscaler protection, and a green or red mark at the right of a tile shows whether the protection is configured correctly or not.

quotes: Each tile shows the name of the technique and the ID.

The tiles highlighted in blue indicate that they are covered by Zscaler protection, and the green or red color at the right side of these tiles indicates whether the protection is configured correctly or not.

framework-legend.statement: The framework page Legend shows a donut chart of techniques covered by Zscaler versus not, with the total percentage of technique coverage at its center, and a Configurations count of misconfigured and correctly configured configurations or policies.

quotes: The donut chart shows the split between the number of techniques covered by Zscaler and those that are not. The center of the donut chart shows the total percentage of technique coverage.
Configurations: This section shows the number of configurations or policies that are misconfigured and configured correctly for your organization.

technique-drawer.statement: In the drawer view for a technique, Zscaler Comment is a note on how Zscaler can help mitigate the attack technique and shows no information if the mitigation strategy isn't available, TTP to Zscaler Product Mapping gives the feature, whether it is licensed and the Risk360 category, and TTP to Risk360 Factor Mapping maps the sub-techniques to factors; in the drawer view for a sub-technique, Zscaler Comment is the same kind of note, and TTP to 3rd Party Tools Mapping shows whether the sub-technique is securely configured, misconfigured, or not covered by third-party security control policies.

quotes: Zscaler Comment: A note on how Zscaler can help mitigate the risk from this attack technique by using one of Zscaler's progressive protection portfolios.
This field shows no information if the mitigation strategy isn't available.
TTP to Zscaler Product Mapping: Maps the attack technique to the Zscaler feature responsible for protecting against these attack techniques

whether the features that are responsible for protecting against these tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) are licensed by your organization or not, and the Risk360 category that the TTP falls under.
TTP to Risk360 Factor Mapping: Maps all the attack sub-techniques to the Risk360 Factors and shows the status of each sub-technique.
Zscaler Comment: A note on how Zscaler can help mitigate the risk from this attack technique by using one of Zscaler's progressive protection portfolios.
TTP to 3rd Party Tools Mapping: Shows whether the sub-technique is securely configured, misconfigured, or not covered by the any third-party security control policies.

technique-search-hover.statement: Techniques can be searched by name or by the mapped factor, and hovering a tile shows the Zscaler Control, Related Risk360 Factors and Licensed?.

quotes: You can search for a technique by its name or the factor mapped to it.
Zscaler Control: The Zscaler feature that is responsible for helping protect against these attack techniques.
Related Risk360 Factors: The Risk360 Factors that are related to the attack.
Licensed?: Whether or not you are subscribed to the Zscaler feature that protects against these attacks.

report-schedules.statement: The Reports page says a new CISO Board Slides slide is generated for a period of 7 days; the Risk Management Mitigation Strategy Report is autogenerated once a week; Operating Entity Risk is a weekly and on-demand report; the Cyber Insurance Addendum is a quarterly and on-demand report.

quotes: CISO Board Slides: The slides provide customers with extensive insight into how Risk360 is helping quantify and measure risk in their network. A new slide is generated for a period of 7 days. The reports are securely stored as a PowerPoint file.
Risk Management Mitigation Strategy Report: A report that outlines the mitigation strategy for important risk factors impacting your organization's risk. This report is autogenerated once a week.
Operating Entity Risk: A weekly and on-demand report for portfolio risk assessment by quantifying risk at the operating entity level.
Cyber Insurance Addendum: A comprehensive quarterly and on-demand report of your zero trust security posture for cyber insurance underwriters.

report-catalog.statement: The Risk360 Reports page (Analytics > Reports > Risk360 Reports) holds CISO Board Slides (a PowerPoint file), an Attack Surface Report, a Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment, SEC Disclosures, Miscellaneous materials, the Risk Management Mitigation Strategy Report, Operating Entity Risk and a Cyber Insurance Addendum.

quotes: You can download various risk-related reports from the Reports page (Analytics > Reports > Risk360 Reports).

CISO Board Slides: The slides provide customers with extensive insight into how Risk360 is helping quantify and measure risk in their network. A new slide is generated for a period of 7 days. The reports are securely stored as a PowerPoint file.
Attack Surface Report: A report that provides you with the details of your organization's exposed applications and servers to a public network
Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment: A report that provides a holistic view of your zero trust journey.
SEC Disclosures: A document with a sample format and content
Miscellaneous: Various materials on risk management
Risk Management Mitigation Strategy Report: A report that outlines the mitigation strategy for important risk factors impacting your organization's risk. This report is autogenerated once a week.
Operating Entity Risk: A weekly and on-demand report for portfolio risk assessment by quantifying risk at the operating entity level.
Cyber Insurance Addendum: A comprehensive quarterly and on-demand report of your zero trust security posture for cyber insurance underwriters.

report-llm-sec.statement: The Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment is generated by a custom large language model developed by Zscaler; SEC Disclosures is a document with a sample format and content that can be a starting point for security and legal teams addressing the SEC's new cyber risk reporting regulations.

quotes: Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment: A report that provides a holistic view of your zero trust journey. It is generated by a custom large language model (LLM) developed by Zscaler.

SEC Disclosures: A document with a sample format and content that can be a helpful starting point for security and legal teams in addressing the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC's) new cyber risk reporting regulations.

framework-method.detail: The framework page article does not state control counts per framework, how a technique is judged covered by Zscaler protection, or how a configuration is judged misconfigured.

report-details.title: Report generation lead time, retention and entitlement
report-details.detail: The reports article does not state how long a report takes to generate, how long generated reports are kept, or which license each report needs.
